name: ID-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a -13 partisan lean
Mike Simpson is a well-funded incumbent with over $1.1M raised
Democrat Ellie Gilbreath raised only about $107K with no outside support
Prediction markets price Simpson at roughly 95% to win
model.rationale: Simpson is a long-tenured incumbent in a district that leans Republican by thirteen points, and he has out-raised his challenger by roughly ten to one. With no polls, no expert ratings flagging the race, and markets pricing a Republican win near certainty, the forecast sits well inside Safe R territory.
model.watch: A major scandal, Simpson's retirement, or a surge of outside Democratic spending would be needed to move this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Idaho's 2nd District is a solidly Republican seat, and Mike Simpson has held it for decades. He enters the general election after easily securing renomination, with a large financial advantage: more than $1.1 million raised and over $400,000 on hand, compared with about $107,000 raised by Democrat Ellie Gilbreath. No independent groups have invested in the race on either side.

The district's thirteen-point Republican lean, the absence of any competitive polling, and prediction markets pricing Simpson's chances around 95 percent all point the same direction. Gilbreath would need an extraordinary shift in the political environment to make this competitive, and nothing in the available evidence suggests one is underway.
